• In the post-absorptive period and starvation the utilization of fatty acids and ketone bodies as fuels by different tissues
replaces much of the need for glucose utilization and is known as “the glucose sparing effect of fat derived fuels”. But since
most of the glucose in starvation is made from amino acids derived from the breakdown of proteins, this could also be
referred to as “the protein sparing effect”.
